title: Polysaccharides; Food tests and chromatography
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM04#t1 term and clue written for the game; BM04#t3 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t4 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM04#N.6, BM09a#N.4a, BM04#N.8, BM09a#N.10, BM04#N.13a, BM09a#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Starch
items.clue: The energy store found in plants

items.label: Cellulose
items.clue: Polymer that gives plants their strong walls

items.label: Reducing sugars
items.clue: Group made up of all monosaccharides plus maltose and lactose

items.label: Biuret test
items.clue: A change from blue to lilac shows that peptide bonds are present

questions.stem: Liver cells store glucose in the form of glycogen. Why is the glucose not simply stored as free glucose?

options.text: Glycogen is insoluble because it is non-polar, so it stays separate from the watery cytoplasm
The branches of glycogen make its glucose hard to remove, so the store is not used up too quickly
Glycogen is relatively insoluble because of its size, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
Glycogen stores extra energy in the glycosidic bonds that link its glucose monomers together

questions.explanation: Glycogen is very large and relatively insoluble, so much can be stored without raising the solute concentration of the cytoplasm. Free glucose would draw water in by osmosis.

questions.stem: A solution gives a negative result with iodine. With Benedict's reagent, heated, it stays blue. A fresh sample is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid, neutralised, and tested with Benedict's again: a brick-red precipitate forms. What does the solution contain?

options.text: A reducing sugar, because the final Benedict's test was positive.
Starch, which the acid broke down into glucose.
A non-reducing sugar, such as sucrose, and no reducing sugar.
A reducing sugar made by the acid joining smaller sugars by condensation.

questions.explanation: Negative first, positive after acid hydrolysis: the acid split a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides.

questions.stem: Cellulose gives plant cell walls high tensile strength. Which feature of cellulose is responsible for this?

options.text: Straight chains lie side by side in bundles, cross-linked by many hydrogen bonds
The glycosidic bonds within cellulose are very much stronger than those within starch
The chains coil into tight helices that stretch and recoil like a spring
Beta-glucose is a larger monomer than alpha-glucose, giving thicker chains

questions.explanation: Straight, unbranched chains of β-glucose pack side by side in bundles linked by very many hydrogen bonds. Each is weak; together they resist stretching.

questions.stem: You have a 10.0 mmol dm⁻³ glucose stock solution. How do you make 10.0 cm³ of a 4.0 mmol dm⁻³ standard?

options.text: 4.0 cm³ of stock + 10.0 cm³ of water
4.0 cm³ of stock + 6.0 cm³ of water
6.0 cm³ of stock + 4.0 cm³ of water
0.40 cm³ of stock + 9.6 cm³ of water

questions.explanation: You need 4.0 ÷ 10.0 = 0.40 of the final volume as stock: 0.40 × 10.0 = 4.0 cm³, made up to 10.0 cm³ with 6.0 cm³ of water.

questions.stem: Humans make amylase, which hydrolyses the 1,4-glycosidic bonds between α-glucose units in starch. Humans make no enzyme that hydrolyses cellulose, which also has 1,4-glycosidic bonds between glucose units. Which explanation is best?

options.text: Cellulose's glycosidic bonds are much stronger than those in starch, so amylase cannot break them.
Cellulose chains are coiled and branched, so amylase cannot reach the bonds.
Cellulose is non-polar, so it cannot dissolve and enzymes cannot act on it.
Its β-glucose units alternate in orientation, so its bonds have a different shape.

questions.explanation: Amylase only fits bonds between α-glucose units. In cellulose, alternate β-glucose units are flipped, so the bond looks different to an enzyme. Cows rely on gut microbes that make cellulase.

questions.stem: A sample of milk is tested. Heated with Benedict's reagent: an orange-red precipitate. With biuret reagent: lilac. With iodine in potassium iodide: stays orange-brown. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: It contains glucose and no other sugar.
It contains starch, protein and a reducing sugar.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable lipid.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable starch.

questions.explanation: Precipitate: reducing sugar. Lilac: peptide bonds, so protein. No blue-black: no starch detected.
